evals.name: infers-and-interviews-before-scaffolding
evals.expected_output: Explores the repo to map the four bundled template patterns (apps, dependency-root, host-wiring, polyglot-services) against what actually exists, then interviews the user one focus area at a time with a recommendation before writing anything. It does not write a focus area file until the user confirms the focus area and its scope globs.
expectations: Explores the repo to draft candidate focus areas from the bundled templates before asking
Interviews the user per focus area with a recommendation, rather than scaffolding blind
Writes focus area files only after the user confirms the focus areas

evals.name: idempotent-reads-existing-areas
evals.expected_output: When .claude/tidy-areas/ already contains focus area files, reads them, summarizes the current focus areas, and proposes additions or edits against that baseline rather than overwriting them blind. It never overwrites an existing consumer focus area without explicit confirmation.
expectations: Detects and reads existing .claude/tidy-areas/*.md before proposing changes
Summarizes the current focus areas and proposes edits against that baseline
Does not overwrite an existing consumer focus area without user confirmation

evals.name: scaffolds-from-bundled-templates-tracked
evals.prompt:
/code-tidying:setup apply

Just scaffold sensible default focus areas for this repo.
evals.expected_output: Fills placeholders from the bundled templates under ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/tidy/templates/ with real repo values and materializes tracked .claude/tidy-areas/<area>.md files. It does not ship or copy template files into the setup skill, and does not write configuration into the plugin directory or a plugin data directory.
expectations: Scaffolds focus area files by filling the bundled templates, not by shipping its own copies
Writes focus area files to the consumer's tracked .claude/tidy-areas/ directory
Does not write configuration into the plugin directory or plugin data directory

evals.name: install-ci-discovers-before-proposing
evals.expected_output: Runs the CI scan and reads the repository's own CI configuration before asking anything, proposes the comment-lint step in the format of the CI system the repository uses (not GitHub Actions by default), matching its existing jobs' conventions, and writes the step only after the user says yes.
expectations: Discovers the CI system and how its jobs get python3, pygments and the change's commits before asking
Proposes the step in the repository's own CI system format rather than a default vendor template
Writes nothing until the user approves the proposed step
